title: Relationship between the flowering of fireweed and climate factors in the Southern Baikal region
abstractText: The onset of phenological seasons in nature reserve complexes is determined by the date of occurrence of specific phenological phenomena. Fireweed is one of the indicator plant species for characterizing the summer phenological season in the Southern Baikal region. This article presents data on the long-term dynamics of the flowering date of fireweed (Chamaenerion angustifolium (L.) Scop.) in relation to air temperature parameters. The study was conducted from 1981 to 2024 in the central part of the northern macroslope of the Khamar-Daban Ridge (protected zone of the Baikal Biosphere Reserve). The consistent trend lines for the fireweed flowering date and the dates when the average daily and minimum air temperatures exceed 10 °C indicate that its development is linked to changes in the regional temperature background. All phenological phenomena showed a consistent tendency toward earlier onset by the end of the study period. Statistical analysis revealed low variability in the fireweed flowering date, the dates when the average daily and minimum air temperatures exceed 10 °C, and the June air temperature (°C). Correlation analysis demonstrates the decisive role of the temperature factor in the fireweed flowering period. Rising air temperatures in June clearly lead to an earlier onset of the flowering phase. A crucial moment for fireweed flowering is the onset of a period when the minimum air temperature is regularly above 10°C, and a similar average daily air temperature is permanently established. The earlier these weather conditions develop, the earlier the fireweed blooms.

Leaf traits diversity of wetland plants in the forest-steppe zone of the Republic of Buryatia
abstractText: Water bodies and streams are an integral component of the Eurasian steppe belt. Despite this, there are few studies of the diversity of leaf parameters in wetland plants under semiarid climate. This study examined the structural and functional parameters of leaves in 22 dominant and most abundant plant community species in the shallows, shoals, and wetlands of Lake Gusinoe, Lake Solenoe, and the Bayan-Gol River in the Selenginsky District of the Republic of Buryatia. It was found that in riparian plants in the forest-steppe wetlands, the most variable parameters were related to leaf blade size – leaf area and thickness, the least variable were dry matter content (LDMC) and leaf density, with leaf specific surface density (LMA) occupying an intermediate position. On average, monocotyledonous species had larger (2.6 times) and thicker (twice as large) leaves with higher LMA (1.6 times) and LDMC (1.5 times) values than dicotyledonous species. The comparative analysis revealed similarities of the modal classes of the studied parameters in wetland plants in the forest-steppe zone of the Republic of Buryatia and Mongolia. Differences in leaf parameters were found between wetland plants and zonal herbaceous plants in the forest-steppe zone of the Republic of Buryatia. Leaves of intrazonal plants were characterized by lower values of the LDMC and LMA modal classes compared to zonal ones, which is related to the reduced impact of arid stress on plants in wetlands.

title: Adaptation features and development dynamics of a number of useful plant species from different geographical zones in the collection of the SEC – Botanical Garden of Moscow State University
abstractText: The article discusses the results of introducing a number of medicinal and economically valuable plant species from different climatic zones, with the aim of growing them in a moderately continental climate as a sustainable source of valuable raw materials (medicinal and fodder resources). The paper examines their potential for adaptation to the natural and climatic conditions of the SEC – Botanical Garden of MSU, including consideration of the seasonal development of the introduced species and the identification of periods of greatest vulnerability within their annual vegetation cycle. The study notes that plant species originating from Northeastern and Central Asia, the Mediterranean, and North America proved to be fairly resilient under the conditions of the “Useful Plants” plot located within the territory of the SEC – Botanical Garden of MSU. Long‑term trials made it possible to assess and rank the studied plant species according to their suitability for the moderately continental climate of central European Russia: Glaucium flavum, Macleaya cordata, and Sida hermaphrodita were classified as promising, while Salvia officinalis was deemed poorly suited. In addition, several valuable medicinal plants disappeared from the collection within a relatively short period: Ziziphora pamiroalaica, Hedysarum neglectum, Rhodiola integrifolia and Rhodiola quadrifida.

title: CRENATE phytoliths of grasses leaves of some cultivated and wild species of Aveninae J. Presl: potential for reconstructing ancient agriculture
abstractText: This paper presents a comparative analysis of the morphometric characteristics of Crenate (CRE) phytoliths extracted from the leaves of wild Aveninae J. Presl species native to the southern part of Western Siberia (Helictotrichon pubescens (Huds.) Pilg., Koeleria cristata (L.) Pers., Koeleria delavignei Czern. ex Domin, Trisetum altaicum Roshev., and T. sibiricum Rupr.) against those of silica particles from selected cultivated and wild oat species (Avena sativa L., A. fatua L., and A. eriantha Durieu). A total of nineteen morphometric descriptors, characterizing both the size and shape of the Crenate phytoliths, were examined. To visualize the differences among species, mean value plots accompanied by standard deviation bars are provided for several key parameters. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was employed as the ordination method. The findings reveal that oat species tend to produce significantly larger crenate phytoliths compared to the wild Siberian grasses. Key morphometric traits – including length, perimeter, and several shape indices (such as compactness, elongation, and aspect ratio) – proved most effective in distinguishing a portion of A. sativa and A. fatua phytoliths from those of other species. Additionally, parameters reflecting lobe expression also contributed substantially to differentiation. Among the wild grasses, T. sibiricum produced the largest forms; however, its phytoliths remained smaller and more compact than those observed in A. sativa and A. fatua.

title: Introduction of rare species of the genus Primula L. in the Botanical Garden of the Irkutsk State University
abstractText: In this article, we present the results of an introduction trial involving three species of the genus Primula L. that are rare in the Irkutsk Region: P. cortusoides L., P. macrocalyx Bunge, and P. pallasii Lehm.; of these, P. macrocalyx and P. pallasii are listed in the Red Book of the Irkutsk Region. The introduction was conducted at the Botanical Garden of Irkutsk State University. Phenological observations were conducted, and the success of the introduction was evaluated using a 100-point scale based on the methodology of A. N. Kupriyanov (Kupriyanov, 1986), taking into account the following indicators: winter hardiness, resistance to diseases and pests, general plant condition, methods of propagation in cultivation, and plant development during the growing season. Based on the study results, all three species were assessed as unequivocally promising. The seeds of the studied species exhibit high rates of laboratory and field germination. The tested species are highly ornamental and show promise for cultivation in the Irkutsk Region. Introducing rare plants into cultivation supports the strategy of ex situ plant conservation.

title: Forms and varieties of cultivated flora in the collection of the section of taxonomy of flowering plants: prospects for use
abstractText: The thematic arrangement of the taxonomic section dedicated to the taxonomy of flowering plants is designed to vividly illustrate the diversity of this species‑rich group of higher plants. The section displays representatives of native flora grown under open‑ground conditions. Enrichment of the world's cultural flora enables the enlargement of the collection with promising forms and varieties that demonstrate greater resilience in cultivation compared to native species. This paper offers a concise overview of the practical applications of perennial herbaceous cultivars in the central zone of European Russia. The focus is on representatives of the following genera: Nymphaea (Nymphaeaceae), Sanguinaria (Papaveraceae), Aquilegia (Ranunculaceae), Dryas (Rosaceae), Aubrieta (Brassicaceae), Erythronium (Liliaceae), Iris (Iridaceae), Cypripedium (Orchidaceae), and Narcissus (Amaryllidaceae). All the mentioned cultivars are widely grown and well adapted to the open‑ground conditions of the region. In addition to their scientific value, they possess high ornamental qualities. This not only extends the flowering season but also enhances our understanding of the morphological diversity within each group. Furthermore, such cultivation helps alleviate pressure on natural populations, particularly for vulnerable and protected species.

title: Prospects for interspecific hybridization of blueberries in Siberia in combination with biotechnology methods
abstractText: Blueberry breeding in Siberia is facing the problem of low winter hardiness of non-district varieties. The paper discusses the prospects of interspecific hybridization using a local species of Vaccinium uliginosum, characterized by high frost resistance, unpretentiousness to soils, early maturation and resistance to diseases as a source of economically valuable traits. The combination of classical crossing methods with biotechnological approaches, in particular in vitro culture, makes it possible to overcome postzygotic barriers, obtain viable hybrids and accelerate the breeding process. Eight varieties of V. uliginosum have been created in the Central Siberian Botanical Garden, and V. uliginosum is being hybridized with North American species (V. corymbosum, V. angustifolium, and semi-tall blueberries V. corymbosum × V. angustifolium). In vitro embryo culture makes it possible to preserve hybridogenic embryos, obtain plants from problematic combinations, and significantly shorten the breeding cycle during remote hybridization, as well as accelerate the breeding process in Siberia. In vitro use ensures effective reproduction of unique genotypes and pre-selection for stress tolerance, which is a promising strategy for creating productive and cold-resistant blueberry varieties for the harsh climatic conditions of Siberia.

title: Dynamics of the content of photosynthetic pigments in the leaves of herbaceous plants under the influence of technogenic pollution in the city of Barnaul
abstractText: The article presents the study results of the content of photosynthetic pigments in 5 species of herbaceous plants: Plantago major L., Plantago media L., Trifolium pratense L., Trifolium repens L. and Taraxacum officinale L. under conditions of technogenic pollution in Barnaul. The patterns of changes in the content of chlorophyll a, chlorophyll b and carotenoids have been identified. Significant differences in the content of photosynthetic pigments in the leaves of herbaceous plants growing in parks, along roads, near thermal power plants, and along river banks have been established. A decrease in the content of chlorophylls has been recorded with an increase in anthropogenic pollution.

title: Growth parameters and leaf functional traits of Pinus sylvestris L. at the juvenile stage of regenerating at the ash dump of the Reftinskaya power station
abstractText: Plant growth parameters, biomass allocation, and leaf functional traits of Pinus sylvestris L. juveniles were studied during natural regeneration on the reclaimed (ash + soil) and non-reclaimed (ash) areas of the ash dump of the Reftinskaya state district power plant (Sverdlovsk Region). It was shown that at this stage of ontogenesis, the seedlings had significant differences in biomass allocation and root system morphology. On the ash substrate poor in nitrogen and phosphorus juvenile plants allocated significantly more biomass to the root system, which was accompanied by an increase in the length and branching of horizontal roots. Changes in the parameters of photosynthetic apparatus were also observed in juvenile plants on the plot with pure ash, which manifested themselves in a significant increase in the leaf thickness and leaf surface area, at lower values of the leaf mass ratio (LMR) and leaf area ratio(LAR), compared to seedlings on the plot soil+ash. Plant growth parameters (plant height and trunk diameter), as well as the mass of the trunk, needles, and the total mass of the plant, did not depend on the edaphic conditions and had similar values for seedlings from different ecotopes. It was concluded that changes in the morphological parameters of the root system, leaf functional traits, and biomass allocation reflect the adaptation of Pinus sylvestris seedlings aimed at maintaining carbon balance and sustainable growth under growth conditions on ash substrates.

title: Strategy for adaptation of tussock to existence in the semi-arid highlands of the Altai Republic
abstractText: This paper analyzes the correlation between the structure of herbaceous shoots and fibrous root systems of the large-bunchgrass graminoids (tussock) life form and the developmental rhythms that determine the adaptation of these plants to the specific habitats of the semiarid highlands of the Altai Republic. With a good water supply, tussocks quickly create a relatively large assimilation surface, ensuring high productivity (pulsed development). This is facilitated by more stable temperatures within the tussock turf than in the surrounding environment, and their relatively weak tolerance to high temperatures is offset by transpiration. When the soil water supply is depleted, tussocks quickly dry out and enter a state of summer dormancy. The ecological characteristics of the tussock life form limit their distribution in the semiarid mountains, where they are typical of the upper vegetation zones with cooler and more humid summers, while in the mountain steppe zone they occupy the most humid habitats.

title: Biological activity of Geranium krylovii (Buryatia)
abstractText: The tannin, flavonoid, and anthocyanin content of Geranium krylovii (Geraniaceae Juss.) was studied. The aim of this study was to determine the content of biologically active substances in the above-ground and underground organs of plants growing in the natural environment of Buryatia. It contains the most tannins compared to other biologically active substances (from 23.87 % to 31.75 % in underground organs and from 16.56 % to 27.32 % in aboveground organs from different growing places); flavonoids – from 0.18 % to 0.24 % in the underground part and from 0.78 % to 0.99 % in the aboveground part; anthocyanins – from 0.03 % to 0.08 % in the root system and from 0.02 % to 0.08 % in the grass. Tannins and anthocyanins accumulate more in the underground parts than in the aboveground parts. Flavonoids are also found in higher concentrations in the aboveground parts of the plant than in the underground parts.

title: Changes in the life form and the rate of ontogenesis in ruderal species of geranium-hedysarum meadows of the northwestern Caucasus
abstractText: In Teberda National Park, a population of field voles (Pitymys majori Thom.) lived in the alpine zone of geranium-hedysarum meadows, creating numerous small-scale disturbances to the vegetation. Some number of ruderal species was occupying these disturbance areas within the community. Wild boar dug up area created large-scale disturbances to the vegetation in the alpine zone. Insolation and drying winds contributed to the mass death of sprouts from the seed bank. Some seedlings of Tripleurospermum caucasicum (Willd.) Hayek managed to survive and subsequently become colony centers for other species. Tripleurospermum caucasicum formed thick, horizontal rhizomes that branch abundantly in all directions. A microclimate was created within the clump, allowing seedlings of other species to establish themselves. The following species colonized: Carum meifolium (Bieb.) Boiss., Anthemis cretica L. ssp. saportana (Albov) Chandjian, Catabrosella variegata (Boiss.) Tzvel., and Hyalopoa pontica (Bal.) Tzvel. In these disturbances Catabrosella variegata and Hyalopoa pontica changed their habitus. Geranium gymnocaulon DC. colonized dug up area no earlier than the 4th year; by the 8th year, the projective cover was 60 %.

title: Structure and dynamics of populations of rare plant species in the Mount Kopeyka Protected Area (Samara Region)
abstractText: The structure and population dynamics of 34 rare plant species growing within the Mount Kopeyka (Gora Kopeyka) natural monument of regional significance in the Samara Region were studied. Data from the authors' studies for the 1999–2000 and 2024–2025 periods were compared. Changes in the number of individuals and the spatial and ontogenetic structure of populations were identified for most of the growing species. A decrease in both the number of individuals and their density was noted for 19 rare plant species. For 12 species, population indicators remained approximately the same, indicating adequate self-sustainment. Only three species (Astragalus macropus, Globularia punctata, and Oxytropis floribunda) showed an increase in the number of individuals and an increase in the density of individuals within cenopopulations, indicating effective self-regeneration. However, the most critical changes in the ontogenetic structure occurred in the populations of four rare steppe plant species: Astragalus helmii, Atraphaxis frutescens, Ferula caspica, and Polygala sibirica. The population status of two species, Astragalus helmii and Polygala sibirica, was considered unsatisfactory. Factors influencing changes in the population structure of rare plant species in the Mount Kopeyka (Gora Kopeyka) Protected Area and their status include livestock grazing, fires, and soil pollution.

title: Adaptation of Pinus sylvestris L. to the alpine tundra climate in the Southern Urals
abstractText: The intensive expansion of tree and shrub species into high-mountain and arctic ecosystems due to global climate change is a pressing issue in modern global science. The rapid invasion of woody vegetation into alpine tundra communities is also occurring in all mountainous provinces of the Urals. In recent years, Pinus sylvestris L., a species uncommon in the Ural highlands, re-established and steadily grown on some peaks in the Southern Urals. Therefore, the adaptation of this species to the extreme climate of alpine tundra is of considerable interest. This paper presents the first analysis of leaf functional parameters of Pinus sylvestris in ecotopes of the Taganai Mountain Range (Southern Urals). The increasing of needles surface area, thickness, and density along the altitudinal gradient, with maximum values in trees from the alpine tundra has been shown. It was concluded that altitude-related changes in leaf functional traits of Pinus sylvestris reflect the adaptation to the highland climate, aimed at increasing the assimilating surface, enhancing light absorption efficiency, and optimizing intra-leaf diffusion of CO2. Under extreme climate, Pinus sylvestris develops the leaf structure that provides high assimilation potential creating the basis for maintaining a positive carbon balance, sustainable growth and functioning.

title: Antimicrobial activity and biologically active substances of Geranium pratense
abstractText: The antimicrobial activity of an infusion of the herb and a decoction of the roots of Geranium pratense L. (Geraniaceae Juss.) against seven opportunistic microorganisms, including Escherichia coli, Salmonella enterica, Proteus mirabilis, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Bacillus cereus, Staphilococcus aureus, Enterococcus faecalis, was investigated. It was found that the herb infusion inhibits the growth of Staphylococcus aureus only, whereas the root decoction inhibits the growth of all seven bacteria tested. The root system of the meadow geranium exhibits more pronounced antimicrobial properties compared to its aerial parts. Plants growing at the edge of a pine forest in Buryatia during the flowering period contain 17.10 % tannins in their above-ground parts and 20.97 % in their underground parts; flavonoids at 1.12 % and 0.14 %, respectively; and anthocyanins at 0.06 % and 0.03 %, respectively.

title: Structure and spatial-temporal variability of phytoplankton in the Ob Bay
abstractText: The study results on the algal flora of the Gulf of Ob are presented. To date, based on long-term research and the analysis of published data, more than 800 algal taxa (at the species and infraspecific levels) belonging to eight divisions have been identified in the plankton of the Ob River estuary. Phytoplankton samples collected during surveys of the Gulf of Ob in the summer and autumn of 2020 revealed high diversity, with a predominance of diatoms, green algae, dinoflagellates, and cyanoprokaryotes. Most species are freshwater, though marine and brackish-water inhabitants have been recorded in the northern part. In terms of structure and abundance, the algal community is diatom-dominated, with the presence of cyanoprokaryotes and dinoflagellates. Moving northward, the community importance of large-celled diatoms and dinoflagellates increases, while cyanobacterial growth declines. Centric diatoms are the absolute dominants in terms of biomass. Phytoplankton development is substantial: abundance reaches up to 32 million cells/l, and biomass up to 10 mg/L. Further north, a decline in phytoplankton vegetative activity is observed. An increase in photosynthesis is noted in the northward direction, resulting from reduced water transparency. The trophic status of the freshwater section of the bay is classified as oligo-mesotrophic, with a slight shift toward eutrophication. The data obtained regarding phytoplankton structure, abundance, and primary production are of both scientific and practical value and can be utilized for biomonitoring purposes.

title: Molecular genetic and biotechnological approaches for the identification and conservation of Tabebuia rosea (Bertol.) Bertero ex A. DC. in vitro
abstractText: Developing protocols for propagating and maintaining Tabebuia in collections in vitro is important for reforestation and urban greening, as uncontrolled deforestation and the removal of plants from natural habitats cause environmental problems and reduce genetic diversity. Forest restoration helps regulate water balance, improve soil quality, and create habitats for many species of flora and fauna. Interest in representatives of the Tabebuia s. l. group of plants is also driven by increased attention to plant species whose tissues contain highly biologically active substances, which are good sources for drug development. In our study, we propose an alternative protocol for micropropagation of Tabebuia on MS nutrient medium supplemented with 2iP. For surface sterilization of seeds, Lysoformin 3000 can be used instead of sodium hypochlorite, which also allows for the production of a large number of sterile seedlings. A comparison of two types of media (WPM supplemented with 4.5 mg/L BAP and 0.2 mg/L IBA and MS supplemented with 1.5 mg/L 2iP) showed that the universal medium supplemented with cytokinin produced normally developed microshoots and allowed them to root on the same medium, while an alternative medium containing a combination of growth regulators sometimes resulted in thickening of the basal portion of the shoots. For the adaptation of rooted plants to in vivo conditions, a nutritious soil proved preferable, ensuring high survival rates, compared to depleted mixtures. Molecular genetic analysis using nuclear and plastid markers confirmed the genetic stability of the culture over several passages and a high degree of similarity to the reference sequences of the species, allowing for confident distinction from closely related taxa. The proposed protocol is promising for mass propagation and conservation, and the markers used can be recommended for routine species identification of representatives of the genus Tabebuia.

title: Effect of actinomycete Streptomyces griseoviridis on plant drought tolerance: an experimental study
abstractText: The relevance of this study stems from the need to find environmentally friendly approaches to increasing the stress tolerance of agricultural crops. The actinomycete Streptomyces griseoviridis is considered as a promising agent. The study yielded a mutant clone resistant to drought conditions in vitro, and its effect on wheat plant (Triticum aestivum) growth in a climate chamber was assessed. The CarD gene, which is involved in the regulation of ribosomal gene transcription and links metabolic processes with stress adaptation, was sequenced. It was shown that the mutation alters the nucleotide composition and structure of the gene and increases the strain's biostimulating activity under high temperatures and moisture deficits.

title: The role of seed coat morphology in the taxonomy of species of the genus Geranium L. (Geraniaceae) of the Altai mountain country
abstractText: The article considers the morphological features of seeds of Geranium species growing in the Altai mountain country. The main macromorphological characters, such as shape, size (length, width, index), seed color, and hilum location, are described; as well as micromorphological characters of the seed coat surface, such as primary sculpture, arrangement, and shape of exotesta cells, features of periclinal and anticlinal cell walls, and secondary sculpture structure. It is shown that the seed coat is exotesta, with sclerified exotesta, its primary sculpture is reticulate-rugose in most species, and bireticulate or microreticulate in some species. Cells of most studied species have an elongated polygonal shape, while in some species they are square-polygonal or rectangular. Their outer periclinal wall is concave, sculptured: secondary sculpture is coarsely, finely, and reticulate-tuberculate. In some species, mamillate tubercles are found on the periclinal walls. Calcium oxalate structures in the form of crystals and druses, as well as wax structures in the form of transverse folds, were also found in some species. The taxonomic role of the studied seed traits – sectional/subsectional and species-specific – is assessed. The studied specimens are presented, along with photographs of the seeds taken using a scanning electron microscope, and a comparative table of macromorphological traits is compiled.

title: The use in ornamental horticulture of plants from family Poaceae breading in Botanical Garden of the Ural Federal University
abstractText: The paper considers the use of plants of the Poaceae family in modern landscape design using the example of cultivars of the Botanical Garden of the Ural Federal University (UrFU). Perennial cereals are valued for their early growth, decorative foliage, aesthetic inflorescences and resistance to adverse conditions. Special attention is paid to two Ural cultivars. The first is Leymus arenarius (L.) Hochst. cv. ‘Gray Ural’ with deep creeping rhizomes, tough bluish-blue foliage, stems 60–120 cm and large light cream ears. It is characterized by winter hardiness, drought resistance, tolerates poor soils, salinity and pollution. It is used for fixing slopes, landscaping of disturbed areas, in curbs, arenas and containers. It remains decorative until October. The second is Festuca pseudodalmatica Krajina cv. ‘Blue Crown’ forms dense rounded bushes 15–20 cm high with bluish-blue leaves and silver-cream panicles. It is durable, hardy, drought-resistant, does not tolerate waterlogging, and is non-aggressive. It is used in borders, rockeries, rock gardens, modular and container gardens, and retains its decorative effect until late autumn. Ural cultivars of Poaceae family make it possible to create aesthetic, low-cost and sustainable urban landscapes. They are durable, decorative all season, do not require complex maintenance and are suitable for a variety of compositions.

title: Spring Flora of the Sunny Island Park Nature Monument (Krasnodar)
abstractText: The article discusses the results of a study of the spring-flowering flora of one of the largest protected areas in the city of Krasnodar, the Sunny Island Park Nature Monument. The field research was conducted using the route method, and the materials of the Scientific Herbarium of the Department of Plant Biology and Ecology at Kuban State University were analyzed. The results of the study were summarized in a list of 98 species, subspecies, and artificial hybrids of flowering plants belonging to 73 genera, 35 families, and 23 orders. When compiling the abstract, the following were taken into account: life forms, habitat range, habitat conditions, and frequency of occurrence. The largest order is Rosales (15 species), which also includes the largest family, Rosaceae (12 species). The largest genus is Acer (7 species). Among the life forms, perennial herbaceous plants (31 species) and trees (31 species) predominate, accounting for 63,26 %. In general, phanerophytes (43 species) are predominant. Introduced species make up a significant part of the studied flora – 16 species (16.33 %). There are also 2 artificial hybrids. In total, 17 geographical elements of the Caucasian flora have been identified, with the Caucasian-European element being the most prominent (15 species). The flora includes a representative of the protected flora of the Krasnodar Territory, Cyclamen coum subsp. caucasicum (K. Koch) O. Schwarz, which has a small population in the central part of the park.

title: Dynamics of plant species constancy in virgin grass phytocenoses on the flat interfluves of the Streletsky site of the Central Chernozem Nature Reserve under absolutely protected regime
abstractText: The article analyzes the dynamics of plant species constancy in three groups of relevés of virgin grass phytocenoses on the flat interfluves of the Streletsky site of the Central Chernozem Nature Reserve (Kursk Region). The first group includes relevés of «original» virgin steppes with regular hay-mowing and pasture use, made in 1928–1934, before the foundation of the Nature Reserve. The second group consists of steppe communities with an absolutely protected regime, described in 1962–1964 and already exhibiting significant signs of transformation characteristic of reserve succession. They are included in the analysis for the first time and are of great interest as an intermediate link of the succession series. The third group comprises phytocenoses described in 2005–2014 in absolutely protected areas. They have lost the signs of steppes and represent fringe vegetation. According to the specifics of the change in constancy over 86 years, plant species are divided into 10 groups (Table 1), for each of which a detailed description is given in the article. To confirm the direction of succession, special attention is paid to the species of three classes: Festuco–Brometea Br.-Bl. et Tx. ex Soó 1947 (steppes), Trifolio–Geranietea sanguinei T. Müller 1962 (fringe vegetation), and Molinio–Arrhenatheretea Tx. 1937 (glycophytic meadows).

title: Morphometric features of panicled hydrangea varieties in the conditions of the Middle Urals, Izhevsk.
abstractText: Specialists in landscape construction recognize representatives of Hydrangea paniculata Siebold as highly decorative shrubs. In the cities of the Middle Urals, these cultures are still rarely used. The purpose of this work is to study the morphological features of shoots and leaves of 6 varieties of H. paniculata growing in the Middle Urals using the example of Izhevsk. According to meteorological data 2021–2022 various weather conditions were observed. It was noted that the deficit of precipitation did not have a big impact on the development of plants. Cool weather conditions of 2022 had a negative impact. The obtained average values of the length and width of the leaf can be considered as morphological feature of the studied varieties, since in different weather conditions 2021–2022 there was a slight change in these values. Groups are defined by the leaf size. Varieties ‘Lime Light’ and ‘Wims Red’ are allocated to the group with an average leaf size (10–20 cm.). The remaining varieties (‘Pinky Winky’, ‘Diamond Runge’, ‘Vanilla Freeze’, ‘Pink Diamond’) belong to the group with small leaves (5–10 cm.). Results of morphological studies were processed using MS Excel programs, Statistica system. The data obtained can be used in landscape construction in the cities of the Middle Urals.

title: Comparative analysis of leaf shapes of Linaria species based on elliptic Fourier descriptors
abstractText: The paper analyzes the shape of leaf blades of four species of the genus Linaria (Plantaginaceae) based on the method of elliptical Fourier descriptors implemented in the SHAPE ver. 1.3 b. The method includes normalization of contours by size, orientation and starting point with the calculation of coefficients up to 20 harmonics, on the basis of which the principal component analysis was carried out with the allocation of 5 components explaining the main patterns of variability. The material was leaves of Linaria acutiloba, L. genistifolia, L. ruthenica and L. vulgaris species in the amount of 100 pcs. (25 for each species) from the herbarium collection of the South Siberian Botanical Garden [ALTB], collected in the Altai Krai, Republic of Altai and Kazakhstan. The results showed the isolated position of all species, especially L. acutiloba, part of L. vulgaris, L. ruthenica and L. genistifolia demonstrate partial overlap of clusters; the revealed deviations are probably due to phenotypic plasticity and the influence of environmental factors.

title: Factors contributing to delays in seeking medical services among diabetic patients in the Kavango East region, Namibia
abstractText: Background: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is a chronic condition that requires timely diagnosis and consistent medical follow-ups to prevent serious complications. Delays in seeking medical services among people living with DM remain a major challenge globally, yet there is limited evidence on the factors contributing to such delays in Namibia. Aim: The study explored factors contributing to delays in seeking medical services among adult patients with DM (both type 1 and type 2) who had a documented gap between symptom onset and first medical consultation at Rundu Intermediate Hospital, Kavango East Region of Namibia. Setting: The study was conducted at a Intermediate hospital in the Kavango east region, Namibia. Methods: The study employed a qualitative, exploratory, descriptive and contextual design. Fifteen purposively selected adults with DM who experienced delays in seeking healthcare participated in semi-structured individual interviews. Data were analysed using inductive thematic analysis. The study adhered to ethical principles, including respect for patients, beneficence and justice. Results: Five major themes emerged: individual factors contributing to delays in seeking medical services for DM; influence of the family and social environment on decision-making; barriers encountered in seeking early medical intervention; healthcare-related factors; and suggestions for improvement. Conclusion: Delays in seeking medical services among diabetic patients at the hospital were largely driven by poor recognition and interpretation of DM symptoms, social influences, and financial and healthcare system-related factors. Early recognition of symptoms and timely healthcare services could prevent avoidable complications and improve outcomes for people living with DM. Contribution: The findings provide context-specific evidence to inform patient education, guide community awareness campaigns and support the development of strategies to improve outcomes for people living with DM in similar settings.

title: Assessment of the raw material base of economically valuable plant species in the Ulytau Region
abstractText: In the context of global climate change and increasing human impact on natural resources, assessing the raw material resources of economically valuable plant species in key regions is essential for the sustainable use and conservation of Kazakhstan's botanical diversity. The cadastral assessment of botanical resources in the Ulytau Region, covering steppe, semi-desert, and desert landscapes and conducted during 2024–2026, continues Kazakhstan's comprehensive botanical investigations. Literature and archival analysis indicate that previous studies in the region have focused mainly on floristics, whereas data on the raw material resources of certain medicinal plant species from the Ulytau Mountains remain limited, localised, and outdated. An updated assessment of these resources is therefore both timely and necessary. This study was conducted in the Ulytau Region, established on 8 June 2022 in central Kazakhstan. The area features hilly uplands, low-mountain terrain, and plains, with a sharply continental and extremely arid climate. Resource assessment surveys identified and quantified the air-dry biomass of 16 economically valuable plant species belonging to nine families. Eight species – Tamarix ramosissima, Euphorbia seguieriana, Galatella villosa, Galatella tatarica, Filipendula vulgaris, Rheum tataricum, Juniperus sabina, Neotrinia splendens – form populations with a potential harvest exceeding 1.0 tonne of air-dry raw material, making them suitable for commercial harvesting. The other species have smaller, localised populations with a potential annual harvest below 1.0 tonne and are recommended for local pharmaceutical use or for seed and planting material collection. A distribution map of these populations within the Ulytau Region was also compiled.

Synthesis of Biographite from Starch Biomass Using Additive Assisted Templating Approach
abstractText: Graphite is a critical mineral with wide-ranging applications in electronics, energy storage, and advanced materials manufacturing. As natural reserves remain limited, there is growing interest in using carbon-rich renewable precursors as alternative feedstocks for synthetic graphite production. Starch, being a widely available, renewable, and carbon-neutral biopolymer, is a compelling, sustainable alternative precursor for graphitic carbon synthesis. However, its inherently nongraphitizable nature requires templating additives to achieve graphitic ordering. In this study, we present a catalyst-free thermal route to produce graphitic carbon from starch-biopolymer-based packing peanuts through carbonization and graphitization, using graphene oxide (GO) and graphene (Gr) as templating additives. The resulting carbon structures were characterized using high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM), selected area electron diffraction (SAED), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and Raman spectroscopy to evaluate the improvements in crystallite parameters La and Lc. At the optimal condition of 2.5 wt % GO loading, crystallite parameters of La = 77.9 nm and Lc = 25.94 nm were achieved, closely approaching those of natural graphite (La = 100 nm, Lc = 24.6 nm). Oxygen content, edge-to-basal oxygen ratio, sp2 π-network, and stacking height are identified as the key factors governing the formation of graphitic or hard carbon from the starch precursor. Unlike conventional catalytic graphitization, this approach requires no metal catalysts, eliminating postprocessing purification entirely. The results establish starch biopolymer as a viable and sustainable precursor for graphitic carbon production.

Aesthetic Rehabilitation of Maxillary Anterior Teeth Affected by Moderate-to-Severe Dental Fluorosis Using Ceramic Veneers: A Clinical Case Report
abstractText: Management of moderate-to-severe dental fluorosis complicated by enamel hypomineralization and intrinsic staining presents a significant esthetic challenge. Conventional conservative therapies, such as microabrasion and bleaching, are often insufficient to mask deep discoloration and surface defects. This case report describes the clinical management of a young adult patient presenting with moderate to severe endemic fluorosis on the maxillary anterior teeth. Following a comprehensive diagnostic evaluation and a direct chairside mock-up, minimal-preparation porcelain laminate veneers were executed from the maxillary right canine to the left canine (teeth #13 to #23). The superficial hypermineralized fluorotic enamel was removed to ensure reliable adhesive bonding. A digital intraoral scanner was utilized for the definitive impression. CAD/CAM-fabricated lithium disilicate restorations successfully masked the underlying intrinsic brownish discoloration while preserving maximal sound tooth structure, achieving a harmonious, functional, and highly esthetic outcome.

Risk of low energy availability among Indian athletes in weight-dependent sports: Phase I multicentre study
abstractText: Low energy availability (LEA) is a concern among athletes, particularly in weight-dependent sports, where high training demands and weight-management practices are associated with LEA risk. This multicentre cross-sectional study estimated LEA risk and examined its associations with exercise dependence, disordered eating, sleep quality, and sleep behaviour among Indian athletes. A total of 271 athletes in five weight-dependent sports (174 males and 97 females; aged 15–23 years) completed the Low Energy Availability in Females Questionnaire (LEAF-Q), Low Energy Availability in Males Questionnaire (LEAM-Q), and validated questionnaires. Overall, 38.7% of athletes were classified as being at risk of LEA, including 51.1% of males classified using the LEAM-Q and 16.5% of females classified using the LEAF-Q ( P < 0.001). LEA risk exceeded 40% among athletes from Delhi andHaryana, junior athletes, those participating in grappling sports, and the middle-weight category. Among female athletes, LEA risk was associated with exercise dependence, disordered eating, sleep quality, and sleep behaviour. Female athletes with disordered eating had 4.4-fold higher odds of LEA risk (OR = 4.42, ​95% CI: 1.08–18.21; P = 0.039), whereas no significant associations were observed among male athletes. These findings suggest considering disordered eating, exercise dependence, and sleep in LEA risk screening.

title: Escaping the understanding-assent links impasse
abstractText: This paper provides an account of radical deviance, of what a speaker must do that would require us to translate her words non-homophonically. The account comes in two parts. The first argues that the appropriate unit of analysis for radical deviance is not a speaker’s utterance of individual sentences considered in isolation from her dealings with other speakers, but her contribution to a meaning-giving dialectic considered as a whole. The second argues that a speaker’s use of a word counts as radically deviant if only if it involves a refusal either (1) to engage in or (2) to respect the meaning-giving dialectic for that word. This account has two important consequences. First, it resolves a longstanding issue with semantic externalism, namely, that of explaining what a speaker must do to get thrown out of the social practice her participation in which secures for her words the meanings they have. Second, it provides a new contribution to the debate over the understanding-assent links thesis, according to which some sentences p are such that, necessarily, whoever understands p assents to p. Williamson (2007, 2012/2020) has argued that there are no such links. Boghossian (2012/2020) and Warren (2021) take themselves to have provided counterexamples to Williamson’s argument. Whether one considers these counterexamples to be genuine, however, is a matter of intuition. Thus the debate is at an impasse. The account of radical deviance proposed here provides a way out.

abstractText: The disconnect in children's reading habits between classrooms and home environments poses a critical challenge to strengthening primary school literacy, particularly within farming communities facing limited reading materials and parental time constraints. This qualitative case study at Detukou Catholic Private Elementary School analyzes school and family involvement, maps supporting and inhibiting factors of reading activities, and formulates opportunities to strengthen literacy networks between home and school. Data were gathered through semi-structured interviews, participatory observations, and documentation involving twenty-one informants selected via purposive sampling, comprising one principal, nine teachers, and eleven parents, and analyzed manually through data condensation, thematic coding, matrix presentation, and triangulation. Field findings reveal that a fifteen-minute morning reading routine and tiered teacher guidance foster initial literacy engagement, whereas afternoon accompaniment by farming parents occurs informally amid work schedules alongside a need for practical guidance and two-way teacher communication. These findings confirm that a reading culture ecosystem in agrarian communities relies on aligning school routines with family time capacities, implying the need for concise home literacy guides and book-lending circulation. ABSTRAK Keterputusan kebiasaan membaca anak antara ruang kelas dan lingkungan rumah menjadi persoalan krusial dalam penguatan literasi sekolah dasar, terutama pada komunitas keluarga pekebun dengan keterbatasan akses bacaan serta waktu pendampingan. Studi kasus kualitatif di Sekolah Dasar Swasta Katolik Detukou ini menganalisis bentuk keterlibatan sekolah dan keluarga, memetakan faktor pendukung serta penghambat kegiatan membaca, dan merumuskan peluang penguatan jejaring literasi antara rumah dan sekolah. Pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui wawancara semi-terstruktur, observasi partisipatif, dan dokumentasi terhadap dua puluh satu informan yang dipilih secara purposive sampling, meliputi satu kepala sekolah, sembilan guru, dan sebelas orang tua siswa, lalu dianalisis secara manual melalui kondensasi data, pengodean tematik, penyajian matriks, serta triangulasi. Temuan lapangan memperlihatkan bahwa pembiasaan membaca lima belas menit pagi dan bimbingan bertahap guru mampu membangun kontak awal literasi, sementara pendampingan sore hari keluarga pekebun berjalan secara informal di sela waktu kerja dengan kebutuhan panduan praktis serta komunikasi dua arah dengan guru. Kondisi ini menegaskan bahwa ekosistem budaya membaca pada komunitas agraris bertumpu pada penyelarasan ritme program sekolah dengan kapasitas waktu keluarga, sehingga berimplikasi pada perlunya penyusunan panduan literasi rumah tangga yang ringkas dan sirkulasi peminjaman buku.
